minutes.headline: Town Meeting defeated moving solar permits to the Zoning Board; passed a Shirley Road rezoning and a parking easement.
minutes.summary: The closing articles of the 2019 Town Meeting. A Shirley Road rezoning passed unanimously, and the Historical Society's School Street parking easement was amended and approved. Articles 40 and 41 were passed over. Article 42, which would have moved solar special permits from the Planning Board to the Zoning Board of Appeals, failed on a counted vote after sharp debate. Article 43 was passed over.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the owners of the corner lots favored the Shirley Road rezoning, and how much land was involved.
A resident asked whether School Street is a public way maintained by the town, and what the Historical Society is.
Spoke on articles 40 and 41, which were being passed over. Welcomed a charrette and community meetings.
Supported moving solar permits to the Zoning Board and said buffer requirements were not enforced.
Described the Planning Board's history with the solar project, a lawsuit, and funds for plantings from the developer.
A Lancaster Avenue resident supported the article because two boards reviewing is good, but disliked how it was presented.
A Planning Board member opposed the article, defended the board's handling of the buffers and called it a power grab.
Opposed the article, said she was fine with how the Planning Board handled it, and objected to casting stones between boards.

votes.motion: Article to rezone Shirley Road parcels to the office park industrial district (needs two-thirds).
Amendment to the easement article, replacing the words 'the point of beginning' with land of the Lunenburg Historical Society.
Citizen petition article 39, granting the Historical Society an easement on School Street.
Article 42, changing the special permit granting authority for solar from the Planning Board to the Zoning Board of Appeals (two-thirds needed).
votes.outcome: failed; hand count 34 yes, 39 no as heard

budget_items.what_was_said: A speaker said the solar developer provided money to plant trees on abutters' private properties.

decisions.decision: The moderator ruled the Shirley Road article covered all four parcels, though the mailed warrant had dropped some language.
Articles 40 and 41 were passed over so a charrette and neighbor meetings could be arranged.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting defeated Article 42, which would have moved solar special permits from the Planning Board to the Zoning Board of Appeals, on a counted vote.
A rezoning of Shirley Road parcels to the office park industrial district passed unanimously, with more than the two-thirds needed.
The Historical Society's School Street easement (citizen petition Article 39) was amended and then approved.
Articles 40 and 41 were passed over so a charrette and neighbor meetings could be arranged.
Article 43 was passed over by voice vote, and the meeting closed.

why_it_matters: Solar special permits stay with the Planning Board, so the same board will keep reviewing solar projects and their buffer requirements.
The Shirley Road rezoning changes what can be built on those parcels, and the School Street easement gives the Historical Society a right over town-adjacent land.
watch_next: The charrette and neighbor meetings promised for the land in Articles 40 and 41, which may return at a later Town Meeting.
